textbookText: 19. (a)To raise the temperature of an object, do you need to add heat to it? If you add heat to an object, do you need to raise its temperature? Explain. 23. A lead bullet strikes a target with a velocity of 500 ms–1. Calculate the rise in temperature
of the bullet assuming that 40% of the heat produced is used in heating the bullet. [Specific
heat of lead = 126 J kg-1K-1]
24. You are designing an electronic circuit element made of 23 mg of silicon. The electric
current through it can add energy at the rate of 7.4 × 10-3 Js-1. If your design doesn't allow
any heat transfer out of the element, at what rate does its temperature increase? (Specific
heat of silicon is 705 J kg-1K-1.)
25. A geologist working in the field drinks her morning coffee out of an aluminum cup. The
cup has a mass of 0.120 kg and initially is at 20.0°C. When she pours 0.300 kg of coffee
initially at 70.0°C what is the final temperature after the coffee attains thermal equilibrium?
(Assume that coffee has the same specific heat as water, and that there is no heat exchange
with surroundings).
